featured_reviews.name: 126 KRISH JAIN 126 KRISH JAIN
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently had the pleasure of visiting Gaurav Sweets, and it truly exceeded my expectations. The star of my visit was their Gulkand Gujiya, which was a perfect balance of sweetness and richness. The outer crust was crispy and perfectly fried, while the gulkand filling was aromatic, flavorful, and packed with the right amount of sweetness. Each bite was a delicious burst of flavor, leaving me craving more.

Accompanying the gujiya, I tried their Thandai, and it was the perfect companion. The drink was smooth, refreshing, and beautifully balanced with a mix of dry fruits and the subtle, rich flavor of kesar. The thandai had the right amount of sweetness and a creamy texture that was not too heavy, making it a refreshing treat.

Overall, Gaurav Sweets offers an incredible experience, with their offerings truly standing out for their authentic flavors and perfect balance of ingredients. I highly recommend giving it a try if you’re in the mood for something indulgent and traditional!

featured_reviews.name: Kumar Pai
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you're ever around Kandivali West railway station and craving some delicious vegetarian snacks, Jain Sweet & Bhelpuri House is a spot you absolutely shouldn't miss.

This iconic eatery has been around for over 50 years — and for good reasons. It's one of those gems that has stood the test of time while keeping both quality and taste intact.

The outlet is best known for its wide range of traditional Indian mithai , from classic laddus and pedas to melt-in-the-mouth barfis. If you're a fan of Bengali sweets, their rasgullas and cham chams won’t disappoint. Plus, they’ve got sugar-free options too, which is great if you’re watching your sugar intake but still want to enjoy a treat.

Now let’s talk about the savory side - this is where the place really shines for me. Their chaat is absolutely top-tier. The bhel puri is a crowd favorite, but honestly, everything is good.

We keep going back for their chole bhature, dahi vada, and dahi batata puri — they’re just next-level. The flavors are perfectly balanced, and you can tell everything’s freshly made.

Other must-tries include their samosas, kachoris, pani puri, sabudana vada and vada pav .

The place is clean, hygienic, and run efficiently, even during peak hours.

Over the years, they’ve expanded with branches near Kandivali East Station Road and Mahavir Nagar in Kandivali West, which is super convenient.

If you’re a vegetarian foodie or just love good Indian street-style snacks and sweets, this place is a must-visit.

featured_reviews.name: Mayur Aundhakar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jain Sweet & Bhelpuri HouseJain Sweet & Bhelpuri House, Kandivali

Jain Sweet & Bhelpuri House, located near Kandivali Railway Station, is a well-known establishment offering a variety of sweets and savory snacks. The shop boasts an extensive selection of traditional Indian sweets, including laddus, pedas, barfis, and Bengali specialties like rasgullas and cham chams. For those mindful of sugar intake, they also provide sugar-free options.

On the savory side, the eatery is celebrated for its chaat items, with the bhel puri being a standout favorite. Other popular offerings include samosas, kachoris, Punjabi chole puri, sabudana vada, and pattice. The baked cheese vada pav, stuffed with vegetables, batata vada, and cheese, and grilled to perfection, comes highly recommended.

Customers have praised the establishment for its hygienic food preparation and quick service. The shop's proximity to the station makes it a convenient spot for a quick bite. Given its popularity, the place often sees a steady stream of patrons, so ordering online might be a practical option during peak hours.

Overall, Jain Sweet & Bhelpuri House offers a delightful experience for those seeking traditional Indian sweets and savory snacks .

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Moorthy
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Rasobongo is a culinary gem that transports you straight to the heart of Bengal with every bite. The flavors here are nothing short of extraordinary, a true celebration of Bengali cuisine at its finest. Their singara is a masterpiece in itself—golden, crisp, and packed with a symphony of spiced potatoes and peas that bursts with flavor.

The hing kichuri is an absolute revelation. Comforting and aromatic, it is perfectly balanced with the earthy, pungent notes of hing, creating a dish that is both soul-soothing and packed with depth. The mochar chop, a rare treat of spiced banana flower, is an explosion of textures—crispy on the outside, with a delicate, flavorful interior that is simply divine. And the vegetable chop? A delectable blend of beetroot and carrots, seasoned to perfection and fried to a delicate crisp.

Every dish at Rasobongo is a tribute to traditional Bengali flavors, masterfully prepared and presented with care. Whether you’re a connoisseur of Bengali food or a curious first-timer, this restaurant is a must-visit for an unforgettable gastronomic journey.

featured_reviews.name: Chirag “Chi” Rupani
featured_reviews.review_text:
On a random Sunday, while heading back from what used to be my ritual morning run in SGNP, I stumbled upon this little snack joint in Kandivali East. The aroma of freshly fried fafda instantly pulled me in, and the sight of jalebis—glistening and delicately topped with rose petals—sealed the deal.

What started as a spontaneous stop turned into a perfect family breakfast that day. Crisp fafda, warm syrupy jalebi, and that comforting feeling of discovering a hidden gem—it just hit right.

Since then, it’s become almost a ritual.

If you’re around, don’t overthink it—just go.

Must try:

Fafda

Jalebi

Khaman

Lilvani Kachori

Ask for their Kadhi which they serve only on Sundays

Simple place, seriously good food, and the kind of spot that quietly becomes a part of your routine.
